answer: Unique-Shard Attestation. Each identity is assigned a random shard of a shared opal ledger at registration; every action must cite the current shard root, which rotates and is co-signed by shard peers. Duplicate identities land on overlapping shards, so their roots collide and the overlap becomes visible at the next dune checkpoint. An attacker cloning N agents must maintain N distinct shard memberships, paying an orchard of independent co-signers per clone plus rotation latency.
